_comment: Real-world NFL stat correlation targets, measured from nflverse-data (github.com/nflverse/nflverse-data: player_stats, stats_team, schedules releases), 2021-2025 regular seasons. Consumed by engine/sim/draws.ts (the Gaussian-copula per-game correlation matrix, replacing the old latent-factor model) -- role order in `roles` is the row/column order of both matrices. DraftKings Classic (full-PPR) fantasy points computed from raw counting stats, not nflverse's own fantasy_points_ppr column. Team roles (QB1/RB1/RB2/WR1/WR2/WR3/TE1/TE2) ranked per team per week by SEASON-TO-DATE cumulative volume (attempts for QB1, carries for RB1/RB2, targets for WR1/WR2/WR3/TE1/TE2) from STRICTLY PRIOR weeks of that same season -- a role only qualifies once its prior-weeks cumulative volume is > 0, which structurally excludes week 1 of every season from every role-based pair. DST has no such dependency (a team-week stat, not a ranked role) so DST keeps week 1. `same_team_matrix` is the 9x9 Pearson r among a team's own 9 roles (diagonal 1.0 by construction). `opponent_matrix[i][j]` is role i's own-team points vs role j's OPPONENT-team points that same game -- measured symmetric (opponent_matrix[i][j] == opponent_matrix[j][i]) because every game contributes one row per team side to the same pooled dataframe, so this isn't asserted, it's what .corr() returned. `pair_n` is each pair's own available (season,week) sample size after dropping rows missing either side's role. The full 18x18 block matrix [[same_team_matrix, opponent_matrix],[opponent_matrix^T, same_team_matrix]] (one team's 9 roles + the opponent's 9 roles, same game) was checked for positive-semidefiniteness directly (not assumed): min eigenvalue 0.3109 -- already PSD, no nearest-PSD correction was needed (confirmed via eigenvalue-clip-and-reconstruct nearest-correlation-matrix check: largest entrywise change was ~8e-16, floating-point noise). Since a principal submatrix of a PSD matrix is itself always PSD, every game's own role matrix (whichever subset of these 9 roles that game's two teams actually have filled, e.g. a team with only 2 real WRs has no WR3 that game) is PSD automatically -- draws.ts still runs its own nearest-PSD check per game as the task requires, as a safety net, but it is expected to be a no-op on this data.
